title: Heuristic kernel selector and attention fusion to cut host overhead
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background:
Hosts spend significant CPU time in kernel negotiation, memory staging, and threadpool contention during prefill/decode for variable-length requests. This ticket introduces a lightweight heuristic kernel selector plus attention-operation fusion and a prioritized host dispatch pipeline to reduce CPU-GPU chatter, redundant memcpy windows, and tail latency.

Problem statement:
- Repeated kernel probing and late kernel selection cause extra round trips and extra memory copies for short-lived inference requests.
- Attention operations for many model variants are executed as multiple kernels resulting in redundant device-to-device traffic and extra host synchronization.
- Host threadpool contention between IO/staging workers and kernel dispatch workers causes jitter and work-stealing overhead.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Heuristic kernel selector: build a compact ruleset + lightweight predictor that picks kernel variant at the host-side based on request metadata (sequence length, kv-cache presence, quantization format, model family) to avoid probing on hot paths.
2) Kernel pre-warm & soft reservation: pre-allocate a small per-GPU fast-path kernel slot for the most-likely variants and pre-warm CUDA/cuBLAS state lazily when selector signals high probability.
3) Attention micro-fusion: introduce fused attention kernels for commonly used heads/configs (causal/decoder-only variants) and a host-level operator that rewrites attention call sequences into a single fused dispatch when model variant supports it.
4) Token-aware dispatch queue: prioritize small, latency-sensitive prefill/decode requests through a separate dispatch lane and use token-bucket backpressure for bulk workloads to limit memcpy bursts.
5) Threadpool soft-affinity and staged pinned buffer reclamation: split workers into IO/staging, compute-dispatch, and eviction workers; enforce soft-affinity to reduce cross-worker synchronization and reuse pinned staging buffers with a bounded LRU.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end 99th percentile latency for short chat requests reduced by >= 15% in the hosted benchmark suite.
- Host CPU user-time for the pipeline path reduced by >= 25% measured on our standard small-seq workload.
- Measured GPU memcpy counts per inference reduced by >= 30% on the fused-attention path.
- Feature gated rollout that can be toggled per-region and per-customer.
- Unit and integration tests cover selector rules and fusion rewrite path.

Implementation notes and decisions made:
- Selector heuristic implemented as a table of rules with a fallback to existing kernel prober. The table is hot-reloadable via config to support fast experimentation.
- Micro-fusion limited to stable model signatures (decoder-only causal blocks) to avoid correctness risks for multi-head cross-attention variants.
- Pre-warm uses a timed lazy-init: allocate and initialize only after N requests in the same second to avoid cold-start waste.
- Token bucket thresholds and lane sizes are configurable and expose metrics for auto-tuning via Optimize subsystem.

Testing plan and metrics to capture:
- Synthetic microbenchmarks: short-seq chat (seq_len 16-64), long-pre-fill (seq_len 512+), batched decode.
- System metrics: host CPU breakdown by thread role, memcpy call counts, kernel launch counts, kernel selection elapsed time, GPU occupancy.
- E2E smoke against hosted API with Canary customers.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime-1.22::heuristic_kernel_selector and runtime-1.22::attention_fusion flags.
- Canary in a single low-traffic region for 48 hours with traffic shadowing.
- Gradual ramp with canaries for Dedicated pools after passing hosted canary.

Observability and telemetry changes required:
- New telemetry events: selector_decision, selector_latency_ms, fused_attention_dispatched, lane_enqueue_time_ms, pinned_buffer_reuse_count.
- Dashboards: selector coverage, tail latency impact by lane, host cpu by worker role, memcpy reduction chart.

Dependencies and risks:
- Dependent on runtime native kernel API that supports fused attention signature (research/ops risk).
- Risk of correctness regressions for fused attention; mitigated by model signature checks and numeric tolerance tests.
- May interact with Dedicated autoscaling policies — need to verify memory pressure when pre-warming kernels.

Next steps:
- Spike: implement selector prototype and micro-fusion rewrite in a branch for one model family (open-gpt-medium) and run synthetic stress tests. Estimate: 3 engineer-weeks.
- Iterate on thresholds and flags based on telemetry.

References and artifacts:
- Design sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/heuristic-kernel-selector (internal)
- Benchmark notebook: drive.google.com/drive/fused-attention-bench (internal)
- Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284 (WIP)
